summary: Depot repair: SSD preservation lapse caused FileVault/BitLocker key mismatch and boot failures on returned devices
description:
Issue summary:
During a routine depot repair in the US-West repair center an SSD swap was performed without preserving or recording the device's encryption metadata. Multiple returned devices (Windows and macOS) failed to boot for end users with either BitLocker recovery prompts or FileVault preboot failures.

Impact:
- 3 end-user devices returned in last 48 hours showed boot-blocked state after depot repair (2 Dell, 1 MacBook).
- Users unable to access corporate laptop until helpdesk intervention.
- Potential exposure of process risk: repair center technicians are not consistently following SSD-preservation or rekeying checklist on encrypted devices.

Environment:
- Depot repair center: repair-center-us-west (internal repair ops).
- Affected devices were corporate-managed and enrolled in MDM.
- Imaging pipeline: SCCM (Windows) + AutoReimage; Jamf (mac) for macOS management.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Device arrives for keyboard replacement; technician opens unit and swaps SSD (replacement or test drive) without recording original drive serial in RMA form.
2) Device firmware S/N and chassis tag are updated in asset system, but drive-level tag mismatch occurs.
3) Device is reassembled and passed through our standard pre-return power-on verification which currently checks POST only (not encryption state).
4) User receives device and on first boot sees BitLocker recovery screen (Windows) or FileVault preboot stuck at login (macOS).

Relevant logs / evidence:
- Windows rescue image logs: manage-bde -status showed "Protection Off" on swap, then recovery required when original drive reinserted.
- macOS console (recovery mode): fdesetup status returned "Encrypted" but preboot plist mismatched; Jamf enrollment device UDID did not match drive serial recorded in depot portal.
- Repair center ticket photos showed swapped drives but missing QR label in RMA form.
- Asset DB audit trail shows drive serial change entries matching the repair technician's handheld scanner timestamp.

investigation: Initial hypothesis: technician workflow skipped drive-level preservation step leading to one of two outcomes: replacement drive left encrypted with different keys, or original drive reinstalled without matching preboot metadata.

Reproduced on bench: performed controlled SSD swap on Dell L7440 with BitLocker enabled. Observed immediate recovery prompt when preboot metadata (TPM PCRs + protector ID) didn't match. Relevant command: manage-bde -status, manage-bde -protectors -get, and event logs (System -> Kernel-Boot).

mac reproduction: swapped 14-inch MBP SSD that had FileVault enabled; fdesetup showkeys and diskutil apfs list showed UDID mismatch; Jamf MDM device record tied to original Logical Drive UUID. Re-enrolling and rekeying required reimaging for clean return.

Root cause: process gap in depot RMA portal and technician checklist — drive-level QR/serial scan was optional and often skipped for quick repairs. Pre-return verification only checked power-on POST, not encryption/preboot integrity.

Contributing factor: lack of automation linking SSD serials to MDM/device records in asset DB. When drives are swapped, the system didn't surface a mismatch to the technician before returning the unit.
Related: linked to INT-50321 (assetdb mismatch) for broader asset normalization issues.
resolution:
Remediation steps completed:
1) Immediate: Contacted affected users and used existing recovery keys (AD-backed BitLocker) to unlock Windows devices; for macOS device performed controlled reimage and Jamf re-enroll. All three devices validated and returned to users.
2) Process: Updated depot repair SOP to mandate drive-level QR/serial photo and scanner capture on intake and before return. Added explicit step to validate encryption status and preboot integrity on the depot checklist.
3) Automation: Deployed a lightweight pre-return script to repair center imaging station that checks for encryption protectors (manage-bde / fdesetup) and compares drive serial against asset DB. If mismatch, ticket is created and device held for SOC/Asset Ops review.
4) Training: Performed a targeted retraining session with depot technicians on 2026-02-28; distributed one-page quick reference.
5) Backlog: Created a follow-up task in automation backlog to add enforced field in RMA portal (cannot complete return without drive scan) and to add an API hook to Jamf/SCCM to surface drive-UID mismatches (ticket INT-161055 created).

Post-resolution verification: Asset Ops ran a 7-day audit of all depot returns and found no additional occurrences after SOP + script deployment. Ticket closed after user confirmation and audit.
